lead: A malposition is a vertex with the occiput not anterior; a malpresentation is any presentation other than the vertex. The presenting diameter decides whether the head can pass: well-flexed vertex 9.5 cm, deflexed OP 11.5 cm, brow 13.5 cm, fully extended face 9.5 cm.
f: Occiput posterior; about 25% in early labour, ROP commoner · Android or anthropoid pelvis, deflexed head, anterior placenta · Backache, long labour, early urge to push, early ROM, swollen anterior lip · Flat lower abdomen, limbs in front; anterior fontanelle felt in front on VE · Presenting diameter occipito-frontal 11.5 cm

sc: Primigravida, 6 cm, severe backache, wants to push early → Occipito-posterior

f: Long anterior rotation about 90%: delivers as OA · Short posterior rotation about 6%: face to pubis, born by flexion, episiotomy · About 4% no full rotation: deep transverse arrest (sagittal suture transverse at the spines, no descent) → manual rotation, Kielland or ventouse if skilled, else CS · Oxytocin only for weak contractions without CPD · Complications: prolonged labour, third-degree tear, PPH

Face: fully extended, denominator mentum, about 1 in 500, submento-bregmatic 9.5 cm; feel mouth with gums, nose, malar bones · Brow: midway, about 1 in 2000, mento-vertical 13.5 cm; feel anterior fontanelle, orbital ridges, no chin · Causes: anencephaly, neck mass, cord coils, multiparity, contracted pelvis, polyhydramnios, prematurity · Head high with a deep groove between head and back

sc: Anterior fontanelle, orbital ridges, no chin → Brow: caesarean

f: Mento-anterior face: vaginal birth by flexion under the pubis; low forceps allowed · Mento-posterior: about two thirds rotate; persistent MP → CS · Face: no ventouse, scalp electrode or FBS · Persistent brow → CS; no forceps, ventouse or oxytocin · Facial bruising and oedema fade in days

tr: Ventouse is never used on a face
sc: Face, chin at the sacrum, no progress → Caesarean

f: Transverse lie presents by the shoulder (acromion); about 1 in 300 at term · Unstable lie keeps changing after 36 wk · Causes: multiparity with a lax uterus (commonest), polyhydramnios, prematurity, twins, praevia, pelvic tumour, uterine anomaly · Wide uterus, fundus below dates, empty pelvis, FHS near the umbilicus · Neglected shoulder: ROM → arm or cord prolapse → obstruction → rupture, death, fistula

sc: Wide uterus, fundus less than dates, empty pelvis → Transverse lie

f: Admit from 37 wk so a CS is ready · ECV from 37 wk; stable transverse lie → elective CS at 39 wk · Early labour, membranes intact: ECV then ARM, otherwise CS · Neglected shoulder: caesarean even if the fetus is dead (vertical incision if needed) · Second twin transverse: ECV or internal podalic version + breech extraction · Compound presentation (hand by the head): leave it, it usually retracts; arrest or cord prolapse → CS

sc: Multipara at term in labour, transverse lie, ROM → Caesarean
Arm out, dead fetus, obstructed → Caesarean, not traction
